transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start: 16:30 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Rivers (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CinderForge CTO), Ravi Patel (CinderForge Sr ML Eng), Samir Khan (CinderForge Infra)

Auto-summary (auto): quick intro, PLG credits, verify hosting options, request security docs and starter scripts

Transcript:
00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, um thanks for joining. this is Maya from Redwood. Owen's here from our se team. how's everyone doing?
00:06 Lena (CinderForge - CTO): good thanks, Maya. we appreciate you fitting us in. short on time but excited to, uh, get a sense for time-to-first-token and the credits you mentioned.
00:15 Maya: perfect. the goal for today is quick discovery — what's your current stack, what you want to ship, and whether you'd go hosted self-serve or need dedicated or private later. then we can land next steps.
00:25 Ravi (CinderForge - Senior ML Eng): quick note: we're prototyping an assistant for our docs and code search. main constraints are latency under 250ms median on gen calls and cost needs to be predictable. we want to try the PLG path first.
00:38 Owen (Redwood SE): cool. for PLG/self-serve you can get free credits, a quickstart SDK, and token-based billing. typical ttft — time-to-first-token — for a dev is under 15 minutes if you follow the quickstart and we can provision sample prompts and a small benchmark to prove latency numbers.
00:52 Samir (CinderForge - Infra): is that with hosted or do we need a VPC? security is a big check for us.
00:58 Maya: totally. most teams start hosted, use the free credits to validate, then either stay hosted or move to Dedicated if they want reserved capacity. Private (VPC/on-prem) is available as well when you need network isolation.
01:10 Lena: okay — what's the difference on day one in terms of changes we need to our infra?
01:14 Owen: hosted is basically API keys and network egress. you'll call our endpoints. for Dedicated you get dedicated GPU pools, and for Private we'd either do a VPC peering or a customer-managed private control plane. Samir, you'd need to open specific egress rules and set up a peering connection for VPC.
01:29 Samir: got it. and KMS? we have an HSM and internal KMS, need customer-managed keys.
01:34 Maya: yep, we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys/HSM in Private. in Dedicated we can also offer integration patterns. I'll share the security pack with specifics.
01:43 Ravi: great. on the model side — do we pick models from your catalog or bring our own? we're experimenting with a 7B and a 13B open model.
01:50 Owen: you can choose from our curated open models in the catalog; we also support user-supplied model files in Private via onboarding. for hosted we have vetted variants and recommended quantization profiles. for prototyping, start with a 7B variant to reduce cost and then if latency allows bump up.
02:05 Lena: latency tradeoffs — how do batching/caching play in?
02:09 Owen: we do automatic KV caching and request-aware batching. with short prompts you usually see better tail latency. there's configuration for batching windows if you have high throughput. for PLG you'll likely keep default low-latency settings.
02:20 Speaker 1: (background) yeah yeah
02:24 Maya: also want to note streaming responses and SDKs — you can do a one-line curl. I'll paste an example in the follow-up.
02:31 Ravi: sweet. what's typical cost for a quick POC?
02:34 Owen: depends on model and tokens, but with the starter credits we usually cover a month of POC traffic for small teams. We can give a cost estimate once you share expected tokens/day.
02:45 Maya: we include PLG credits to get you to first meaningful metric — time-to-first-token basically means you can do your first request and see responses in minutes.
02:55 Lena: that sounds good. we have compliance questions — SOC 2, audit logs, SSO/SAML.
03:00 Maya: we are SOC 2 type II and provide audit logs, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and RBAC. I'll include the SOC2 cert and our audit log format.
03:10 Samir: do you expose detailed request logs with token-level breakdowns? we need to tie costs back to features.
03:15 Owen: console exposes token-level cost and per-route latency. for Private deployments, logs can be exported to your SIEM.
03:23 Ravi: question about model rollouts — can you do canary and automatic fallback? we want to route to cheaper variants when load spikes.
03:29 Owen: yes, rollout features: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to compatible model variants. also smart routing by region and cost.
03:38 Maya: any blockers today to get started with credits?
03:41 Lena: internal approval but we can approve a small PLG credit allocation. need the security pack to send to infosec.
03:46 Maya: ok I'll send that after the call. Owen will send a starter benchmark and prompts.
03:52 Ravi: for the benchmark — can you include a small harness that runs concurrency 8 and single-request latency metrics? and a few realistic prompts from our codebase?
03:59 Owen: yes, we'll include a harness with concurrency, simple lat/throughput scripts, and example curl and python sdk snippets. we'll also include a sample prompt set.
04:10 Lena: is there support for early cost optimization — quantization, caching suggestions?
04:14 Owen: Redwood Optimize includes recommendations for batching, quantization profiles, and cache/window suggestions. we also provide a cost breakdown per-token in the console so you can iterate.
04:24 Samir: if we go Dedicated, what's the lead time and commitment?
04:28 Maya: Dedicated lead time is usually a couple of weeks once contract is signed and capacity reserved; commitment models vary monthly/annual. for most PLG-first companies they stay hosted for POC then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput.
04:40 Lena: any partners or vendor lock-in we should worry about?
04:43 Maya: we aim to keep things standard — SDKs are open and models are standard formats; export paths are available. lock-in risk is low if you keep model prompts portable.
04:52 Ravi: competitor question — how do you compare to Lambda Labs or OpenAI for latency/cost?
04:56 Owen: Lambda Labs is great for self-hosted infra but doesn't provide the unified control plane and PLG API. OpenAI has strong hosted offering but different pricing and less emphasis on dedicated/private deployments. Redwood focuses on predictable inference economics and operational controls.
05:12 Maya: any legal procurement needs we should prep for?
05:15 Lena: standard — paperwork, terms of service, and a scoping doc for pilot. Infosec will want a diagram.
05:22 Maya: cool. we'll send a scoping doc and diagram along with the security pack.
05:27 (short pause)
05:30 Ravi: one more technical: do you support streaming function/tool calling and structured outputs? some of our flows need function calling for traceability.
05:38 Owen: yes, streaming responses and function/tool calling are supported; structured outputs with schema validation are supported in the SDK.
05:44 Samir: networking — for VPC peering do you support cross-account peering and route tables?
05:48 Maya: yes, Private supports cross-account peering patterns, and we'll include network diagrams. Samir, if you share CIDR ranges we'll validate.
05:57 Lena: timeline — assuming we get credits and the security review passes, when can we run the benchmark?
06:02 Maya: Owen can send the scripts 48 hours, you can run in your environment or hosted. if you run hosted, we can provide a seeded dataset and credits so you can be done in a day.
06:12 Owen: we'll aim to get the artifacts out today or tomorrow.
06:15 Maya: okay let's recap — I'll send security docs, SOC2, and pricing. Owen will send benchmark harness, prompts, and curl/python snippets. Ravi and Samir will confirm target prompts and infra CIDRs.
06:27 Lena: sounds good. last thing — does Redwood do SSO SCIM provisioning?
06:30 Maya: yes we support SCIM for user provisioning, SAML/OIDC for SSO.
06:36 Ravi: perfect. any blockers on your side?
06:38 Owen: no blockers. we'll include an example quickstart that should get your engineers to first request in under 15 minutes.
06:45 Maya: great thanks everyone. we'll follow up with docs and links.
06:48 Lena: thanks, appreciate it.
06:50 (call ends)
